import Mathlib

inductive BinarySearchTree : Type
| Empty : BinarySearchTree
| Node : Int → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree

def view (t : BinarySearchTree) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => ∅
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_bst (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => True
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def delete_precond (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_bst t
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- `delMin v l r` removes the minimum element of the (nonempty) tree
    `Node v l r`, returning that minimum together with the remaining tree. -/
def delMin (v : Int) (l r : BinarySearchTree) : Int × BinarySearchTree :=
  match l with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => (v, r)
  | BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll lr =>
      let p := delMin lv ll lr
      (p.1, BinarySearchTree.Node v p.2 r)

/-- Naive BST deletion: search for `v`; when found, either splice out the node
    (if the right subtree is empty) or replace its value by the minimum of the
    right subtree, which is removed from there. -/
def delAux (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) : BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => BinarySearchTree.Empty
  | BinarySearchTree.Node w l r =>
      if v < w then BinarySearchTree.Node w (delAux l v) r
      else if w < v then BinarySearchTree.Node w l (delAux r v)
      else
        match r with
        | BinarySearchTree.Empty => l
        | BinarySearchTree.Node rv rl rr =>
            let p := delMin rv rl rr
            BinarySearchTree.Node p.1 l p.2
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def delete (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : delete_precond t v) : BinarySearchTree :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  delAux t v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def delete_postcond (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) (result : BinarySearchTree)
    (_ : delete_precond t v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_bst result ∧
  view result = view t \ {v}
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem set_helper_left (A B : Set Int) (w v : Int) (hB : v ∉ B) (hw : v ≠ w) :
    (A \ {v}) ∪ B ∪ {w} = (A ∪ B ∪ {w}) \ {v} := by
  ext x
  by_cases hx : x = v
  · subst hx
    simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_diff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, hB, hw]
    simp [hB, hw]
  · simp [hx]

theorem set_helper_right (A B : Set Int) (w v : Int) (hA : v ∉ A) (hw : v ≠ w) :
    A ∪ (B \ {v}) ∪ {w} = (A ∪ B ∪ {w}) \ {v} := by
  ext x
  by_cases hx : x = v
  · subst hx
    simp [hA, hw]
  · simp [hx]

theorem set_helper_leaf (A : Set Int) (w : Int) (hA : w ∉ A) :
    A = (A ∪ (∅ : Set Int) ∪ {w}) \ {w} := by
  ext x
  by_cases hx : x = w
  · subst hx
    simp [hA]
  · simp [hx]

theorem set_helper_two (A C : Set Int) (m w : Int) (hA : w ∉ A) (hC : w ∉ C)
    (hm : w ≠ m) :
    A ∪ C ∪ {m} = (A ∪ (C ∪ {m}) ∪ {w}) \ {w} := by
  ext x
  by_cases hx : x = w
  · subst hx
    simp [hA, hC, hm]
  · simp [hx]

theorem set_helper_assoc (A B : Set Int) (v m : Int) :
    (A ∪ {m}) ∪ B ∪ {v} = (A ∪ B ∪ {v}) ∪ {m} := by
  ext x
  simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  tauto

theorem delMin_spec : ∀ (l : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int) (r : BinarySearchTree),
    is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node v l r) →
    is_bst (delMin v l r).2 ∧
    view (BinarySearchTree.Node v l r) = view (delMin v l r).2 ∪ {(delMin v l r).1} ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view (delMin v l r).2, (delMin v l r).1 < x) := by
  intro l
  induction l with
  | Empty =>
    intro v r h
    simp only [is_bst] at h
    obtain ⟨hl, hbl, hr, hbr⟩ := h
    refine ⟨hbr, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simp only [delMin, view]
      ext x
      simp
    · intro x hx
      simp only [delMin] at hx
      exact hr x hx
  | Node lv ll lr ihll _ =>
    intro v r h
    simp only [is_bst] at h
    obtain ⟨hl, hbl, hr, hbr⟩ := h
    have IH := ihll lv lr hbl
    obtain ⟨IH1, IH2, IH3⟩ := IH
    have hkey : delMin v (BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll lr) r =
        ((delMin lv ll lr).1, BinarySearchTree.Node v (delMin lv ll lr).2 r) := by
      simp [delMin]
    rw [hkey]
    have hmem : (delMin lv ll lr).1 ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll lr) := by
      rw [IH2]; simp
    have hmv : (delMin lv ll lr).1 < v := hl _ hmem
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simp only [is_bst]
      refine ⟨?_, IH1, hr, hbr⟩
      intro x hx
      apply hl
      rw [IH2]
      exact Or.inl hx
    · have hv : view (BinarySearchTree.Node v (BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll lr) r)
          = view (BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll lr) ∪ view r ∪ {v} := rfl
      have hv2 : view (BinarySearchTree.Node v (delMin lv ll lr).2 r)
          = view (delMin lv ll lr).2 ∪ view r ∪ {v} := rfl
      rw [hv, hv2, IH2]
      exact set_helper_assoc _ _ _ _
    · intro x hx
      simp only [view, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
      rcases hx with (hx | hx) | hx
      · exact IH3 x hx
      · have := hr x hx
        omega
      · omega

theorem delAux_spec : ∀ (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int), is_bst t →
    is_bst (delAux t v) ∧ view (delAux t v) = view t \ {v} := by
  intro t
  induction t with
  | Empty =>
    intro v _
    refine ⟨by simp [delAux, is_bst], ?_⟩
    simp only [delAux, view]
    simp
  | Node w l r ihl ihr =>
    intro v h
    simp only [is_bst] at h
    obtain ⟨hl, hbl, hr, hbr⟩ := h
    by_cases h1 : v < w
    · obtain ⟨il, vl⟩ := ihl v hbl
      have hvr : v ∉ view r := by
        intro hx
        have := hr v hx
        omega
      have hne : v ≠ w := by omega
      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · simp only [delAux, if_pos h1, is_bst]
        refine ⟨?_, il, hr, hbr⟩
        intro x hx
        rw [vl] at hx
        exact hl x hx.1
      · simp only [delAux, if_pos h1, view, vl]
        exact set_helper_left _ _ _ _ hvr hne
    · by_cases h2 : w < v
      · obtain ⟨ir, vr⟩ := ihr v hbr
        have hvl : v ∉ view l := by
          intro hx
          have := hl v hx
          omega
        have hne : v ≠ w := by omega
        refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
        · simp only [delAux, if_neg h1, if_pos h2, is_bst]
          refine ⟨hl, hbl, ?_, ir⟩
          intro x hx
          rw [vr] at hx
          exact hr x hx.1
        · simp only [delAux, if_neg h1, if_pos h2, view, vr]
          exact set_helper_right _ _ _ _ hvl hne
      · have hvw : v = w := by omega
        subst hvw
        clear h1 h2
        cases r with
        | Empty =>
          have hnl : v ∉ view l := by
            intro hx
            have := hl v hx
            omega
          refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
          · simp only [delAux, lt_irrefl, if_neg (lt_irrefl v)]
            exact hbl
          · simp only [delAux, if_neg (lt_irrefl v), view]
            exact set_helper_leaf _ _ hnl
        | Node rv rl rr =>
          have S := delMin_spec rl rv rr hbr
          obtain ⟨S1, S2, S3⟩ := S
          have hmem : (delMin rv rl rr).1 ∈
              view (BinarySearchTree.Node rv rl rr) := by
            rw [S2]; simp
          have hmv : v < (delMin rv rl rr).1 := hr _ hmem
          have hkey : delAux (BinarySearchTree.Node v l
              (BinarySearchTree.Node rv rl rr)) v =
              BinarySearchTree.Node (delMin rv rl rr).1 l (delMin rv rl rr).2 := by
            simp [delAux]
          rw [hkey]
          have hnl : v ∉ view l := by
            intro hx
            have := hl v hx
            omega
          have hnp : v ∉ view (delMin rv rl rr).2 := by
            intro hx
            have : v ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node rv rl rr) := by
              rw [S2]; exact Or.inl hx
            have := hr v this
            omega
          refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
          · simp only [is_bst]
            refine ⟨?_, hbl, S3, S1⟩
            intro x hx
            have := hl x hx
            omega
          · have hv : view (BinarySearchTree.Node v l
                (BinarySearchTree.Node rv rl rr))
                = view l ∪ view (BinarySearchTree.Node rv rl rr) ∪ {v} := rfl
            have hv2 : view (BinarySearchTree.Node (delMin rv rl rr).1 l
                (delMin rv rl rr).2)
                = view l ∪ view (delMin rv rl rr).2 ∪ {(delMin rv rl rr).1} := rfl
            rw [hv, hv2, S2]
            exact set_helper_two _ _ _ _ hnl hnp (by omega)
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem delete_postcond_satisfied (t : BinarySearchTree) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : delete_precond t v) :
    delete_postcond t v (delete t v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  exact delAux_spec t v h_precond
  -- !benchmark @end proof

`LEAN VERIFIED`.

## What I implemented

**`auxcode`** — two helpers:
- `delMin v l r`: structural recursion on the left spine; returns the minimum of the nonempty tree `Node v l r` together with the tree minus that minimum.
- `delAux t v`: the naive BST delete — compare with the node value, recurse left/right, and on a match either splice out the node (empty right subtree) or replace its value with the right subtree's minimum, removed from there.

**`code`** — `delAux t v` (the precondition witness isn't needed for computation, only for the proof).

**`lemma`** — four small set-algebra lemmas plus the two real workhorses:
- `delMin_spec`: by induction on the left subtree, generalizing the node value and right subtree, gives `is_bst (delMin …).2`, `view (Node v l r) = view (delMin …).2 ∪ {min}`, and `∀ x ∈ remainder, min < x`.
- `delAux_spec`: by induction on the tree, gives both postcondition conjuncts.

**`proof`** — `exact delAux_spec t v h_precond`.

## Semantic audit

- **Precondition** `is_bst t` is genuinely consumed: `delAux_spec` takes it as a hypothesis and it's needed in every branch (e.g. to know `v ∉ view r` when `v < w`, and that the right subtree's minimum exceeds the deleted node's value).
- **Both postcondition conjuncts** are proved as stated, unmodified: `is_bst result` and `view result = view t \ {v}`.
- **Algorithm is the requested one.** No sorting, no specification oracle, no brute force, no `Nat.find`/`Classical.choose`/`decide`. `delMin` genuinely returns the minimum — this is established, not assumed: the lemma proves the returned element is strictly below every element remaining in the tree.
- **Edge cases**: empty tree deletes to empty; a value absent from the tree leaves `view` unchanged (`view t \ {v} = view t` holds since `v ∉ view t`); deleting a leaf, a node with only a left child (`r = Empty` branch returns `l`), and a node with two children (min-of-right-subtree branch) are all handled and all appear as separate proof cases. Values are `Int`, so all-negative inputs are no different from any other — nothing in the code or proofs assumes non-negativity or a sentinel value.
- **No placeholder definitions**: every helper is a real construction with a real proof; no `:= 0`, no `:= True`, no `sorry`/`admit`/`axiom`/`partial`/`unsafe` in the editable sections. The teacher-provided regions and all six marker pairs are unchanged.

Remaining output is warnings only (two unused-variable notes on teacher-provided signatures, and two redundant `simp` arguments in a helper lemma).

analysis:
The student’s submission does satisfy the semantic requirements of the problem.

What the problem asked for:
- implement a Binary Search Tree representing a mathematical set,
- focus on the delete operation,
- use a BST-style delete (the prompt explicitly allows the naive BST delete),
- prove:
  1. the resulting tree preserves the BST invariant,
  2. the resulting set is the old set minus the deleted value,
- and avoid cheating tricks such as `sorry`, `admit`, empty bodies, or delegating to pre-existing verified implementations.

What the student implemented:
- A custom inductive tree type:
  - `Empty`
  - `Node : Int → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree`
- A set model `view` mapping the tree to a `Set Int`.
- A BST invariant `is_bst` stating:
  - all elements in the left subtree are `< v`,
  - all elements in the right subtree are `> v`,
  - both subtrees are BSTs.

Delete algorithm:
- They define `delAux`, which is a standard naive BST deletion algorithm:
  - if target `v < w`, recurse into the left subtree;
  - else if `w < v`, recurse into the right subtree;
  - else found the node:
    - if right subtree is empty, return left subtree;
    - otherwise replace the node’s value with the minimum element from the right subtree, removing that minimum via `delMin`.
- They define `delMin` explicitly from scratch, recursively descending left until the minimum is found.

This is exactly a standard naive BST delete, and it matches the natural language requirement.

Proof obligations:
- They prove `delMin_spec`, establishing the expected structural/set properties of `delMin`.
- They prove `delAux_spec`, showing:
  - `is_bst (delAux t v)`,
  - `view (delAux t v) = view t \ {v}`.
- The final theorem `delete_postcond_satisfied` directly uses `delAux_spec`.

Cheating check:
- No `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, or placeholder bodies.
- No use of built-in tree deletion or set deletion algorithms to bypass the implementation task.
- The delete algorithm is genuinely implemented by recursion over the custom BST.
- The proofs are present and nontrivial.

One minor note:
- The student models sets via `view` using unions and singleton insertion, so duplicate values would collapse in the model. But the BST invariant uses strict inequalities, which is consistent with set semantics and standard BST uniqueness. This is aligned with the task.

Overall, the student implemented the required BST delete algorithm from scratch and proved the intended properties, without obvious cheating.
